questions.question: Describe the steps for reading a graph correctly.
questions.expected_answer: First read the title to know what the graph is about, its date and source. Then read the labels on the horizontal and vertical axes. Check the scale and units, for example whether numbers are in thousands or millions. Read the value of each bar or point by following it across to the scale. Finally, compare the values to find the highest, the lowest and any patterns. Bar graphs compare categories, line graphs show change over time and pie charts show parts of a whole.

questions.question: Describe the population of the provinces according to the 2022 census, and how South Africa's population has changed.
questions.expected_answer: Gauteng had the most people, about fifteen million, followed by KwaZulu-Natal with about twelve million, then the Western Cape with about seven point four million and the Eastern Cape with about seven point two million. Limpopo, Mpumalanga, North West and the Free State had fewer, and the Northern Cape had the fewest, about one point four million. South Africa's population grew from about forty-one million in 1996 to about sixty-two million in 2022.

questions.question: Explain why the province with many people is not always the most densely populated, using examples.
questions.expected_answer: Density depends on both population and area. The Eastern Cape has many people, but it is a large province, so its density is only roughly forty people per square kilometre, lower than smaller KwaZulu-Natal at about one hundred and thirty. Gauteng has the most people on the smallest area, so its density is over eight hundred per square kilometre, while the Northern Cape, the largest province with the fewest people, has only about three or four.
